governanceNotes: D1 batch 45 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - hip labral tear to post-traumatic osteoarthritis (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION (chondrolabral-junction failure and altered hip-joint load), matching the shoulder bankart-lesion and hill-sachs-lesion precedent for structural labral/articular lesions. The proposition rests on the Dean 2024 minimum-eight-year hip-arthroscopy cohort, which associates chondrolabral junction breakdown with conversion to total hip arthroplasty after arthroscopic treatment of symptomatic labral tears, and on the Martin 2024 randomized trial of hip arthroscopy versus physical therapy for symptomatic acetabular labral tears in patients older than 40 years, which reports conversion to total hip arthroplasty among the outcome measures. The edge is not raised to causation: both sources are treatment cohorts in which arthroplasty conversion is a composite clinical endpoint rather than a direct osteoarthritis-incidence measurement, labral tears are themselves frequently a manifestation of established hip degeneration (direction can run the other way), and age, femoroacetabular morphology, and baseline cartilage grade are strong confounders, so no probability estimate is asserted.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Hip-arthroscopy cohorts document that chondrolabral damage accompanying symptomatic labral tears is associated with progressive hip-joint degeneration: the Dean 2024 minimum-eight-year cohort associates chondrolabral junction breakdown with conversion to total hip arthroplasty after arthroscopic treatment of labral tears, and the Martin 2024 randomized trial reports conversion to total hip arthroplasty among the outcomes of treating symptomatic acetabular labral tears - a reproducible lesion-to-arthropathy association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located evidence comprises treatment cohorts in which arthroplasty conversion is a composite clinical endpoint rather than a direct osteoarthritis-incidence measurement, labral tears are frequently themselves a manifestation of established hip degeneration so the direction can be reversed, and age, femoroacetabular morphology, and baseline cartilage grade are strong confounders, so an individual determination requires documentation of the tear and the articular cartilage, chronology, and exclusion of competing arthropathies.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized biomechanical route is described: a tear of the acetabular labrum and the adjacent chondrolabral junction compromises the labrum's role in sealing the joint, distributing load, and maintaining hip-joint fluid-film lubrication, so the acetabular cartilage is exposed to higher and more edge-loaded contact stresses that can initiate and propagate degeneration and lead to arthroplasty - the mechanism under which the located hip-arthroscopy cohorts associate chondrolabral-junction breakdown with conversion to total hip arthroplasty; the treatment-cohort design, the reverse-direction possibility, and the confounding by age and femoroacetabular morphology leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Concurrent femoroacetabular morphology, gluteal or capsular insufficiency, and prior hip injury or surgery can redistribute load further, and the surgical intervention itself alters joint mechanics, complicating attribution.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: the located evidence is hip-arthroscopy treatment cohorts associating chondrolabral damage with arthroplasty conversion, an endpoint that reflects composite clinical deterioration rather than measured osteoarthritis incidence, and labral tears can be a consequence as well as a precursor of hip degeneration, with age and joint morphology confounding the relationship; an individual claim therefore requires tear and cartilage documentation, chronology, and competing-cause review, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Imaging or arthroscopic documentation of the hip labral tear (location, grade, date); documentation of acetabular and femoral articular cartilage status at the time of the tear; chronology of the tear relative to the onset and progression of degenerative change; characterization of femoroacetabular morphology, hip dysplasia, or prior trauma or surgery; evaluation for primary osteoarthritis, inflammatory arthritis, and crystalline arthropathy; orthopedic assessment of whether the labral tear materially contributed to the individual arthropathy
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: hip-arthroscopy cohorts document that chondrolabral-junction breakdown in symptomatic labral tears is associated with conversion to total hip arthroplasty, and a randomized trial of labral-tear treatment reports arthroplasty conversion among its outcomes, establishing a reproducible association between labral/chondrolabral damage and hip-joint degeneration; the edge is not raised to causation because the evidence comprises treatment cohorts with a composite endpoint, labral tears may be a consequence of established degeneration, and age and joint morphology are strong confounders, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with tear, cartilage, chronology, and competing-cause requirements; no probability estimate is asserted.
